extracted.intended_audience: editors, bibliographers, literary scholars, and readers compiling short-story indices and magazine rankings (1914–1915)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and metrics for identifying, classifying, and ranking short stories and periodicals in the Yearbook's 1914–1915 index; includes which magazines are in scope, how distinction is marked, counting conventions, selection thresholds, and tie-breaking. Intended to standardize inclusion and presentation of short-story data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction system
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, and three asterisks are employed to indicate relative distinction. 'Three-asterisk stories' are of somewhat permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-asterisk stories entitle the title to a place on the annual 'Roll of Honor.' Use one, two, or three asterisks to mark relative levels of distinction beside story titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of magazines included
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes the averages of all American magazines published during 1915 of which complete files for the period covered were placed at my disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only magazines for which the compiler had complete files for the covered period are included in the averages and comparative tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of reprints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts of stories and any rankings expressly omit reprinted material; only original publications within the period are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary numeric metrics recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables include: No. of Stories Published; No. of Distinctive Stories Published; Percentage of Distinctive Stories Published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three columns form the basis for magazine comparison and ranking in the Yearbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection threshold for ranked subset
rubrics_metrics.description: The tables indicate the rank, during 1913, by number and percentage of distinctive stories published, of the eighteen periodicals coming within the scope of my examination which have published during the past year over twenty-five stories and which have exceeded an average of 13% in stories of distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To appear in this ranked subset a periodical must (a) have published more than 25 stories during the year and (b) have an average of at least 13% stories marked as distinctive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in the above lists have been decided by taking relative rank in other lists into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two or more periodicals tie on a given metric, compare their positions across the other metric lists (e.g., number vs. percentage) to resolve the tie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing by two-asterisk counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The following periodicals have published during 1915 ten or more 'two-asterisk stories.' The list excludes reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodicals meeting the threshold (≥10 two-asterisk stories) are enumerated; this is a separate count-based recognition distinct from percentage rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing by three-asterisk counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The following periodicals have published during 1915 three or more 'three-asterisk stories.' The list excludes reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodicals with ≥3 three-asterisk stories are listed to identify those publishing multiple works of lasting literary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index coverage — full listing by year
rubrics_metrics.description: All short stories published in the following magazines during 1914 are listed: Atlantic Monthly, Harper's Magazine, Century Magazine, Metropolitan Magazine, Collier's Weekly, Saturday Evening Post, Forum, Scribner's Magazine. All short stories published in the following magazines and newspapers during 1915 are indexed: (long list follows in text: American Magazine; Associated Sunday Magazines (Jan.–May, excluding Every Week); Atlantic Monthly; Harper's Weekly; Bellman; Illustrated Sunday Magazine; Boston Evening Transcript; International; Boston Daily Advertiser; Ladies' Home Journal; Bruno Chap Books; Lippincott's Magazine; Century Magazine; Little Review; Collier's Weekly; McBride's Magazine; Delineator; McClure's Magazine; Everybody's Magazine; Masses; Every Week; Metropolitan; Fabulist; Midland; Forum; National Sunday Magazine; Harper's Bazar; New Republic; Harper's Magazine; Outlook; Pictorial Review; Scribner's Magazine; Reedy's Mirror; Sunset Magazine; Saturday Evening Post.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Yearbook provides complete indices for the named magazines in the specified years; consult the stated magazine lists to determine whether a magazine's entire output is indexed for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index coverage — 'distinction only' listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories, of distinction only, published in the following magazines during 1915 are indexed: Black Cat; Hearst's Magazine; Bruno's Weekly; Life; Chicago Sunday Tribune; Munsey's Magazine; Cosmopolitan; Smart Set; Good Housekeeping; Woman's Home Companion; Greenwich Village.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these periodicals only stories marked with one or more asterisks (i.e., 'stories of distinction') are included in the index; non-distinguished items are omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index abbreviation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The following abbreviations are used in the index (examples given): Am = American Magazine; A.S.M = Associated Sunday Magazines; Atl = Atlantic Monthly; B.C = Black Cat; B.C.B = Bruno Chap Books; B.D.A = Boston Daily Advertiser; Bel = Bellman; B.E.T = Boston Evening Transcript; Brun. W = Bruno's Weekly; Cen = Century Magazine; Ch. Trib = Chicago Sunday Tribune; Col = Collier's Weekly; Cos = Cosmopolitan Magazine; Del = Delineator; Ev = Everybody's Magazine; E.W = Every Week; Fab = Fabulist; For = Forum; G.H = Good Housekeeping; G.V = Greenwich Village; Harp. B = Harper's Bazar; Harp. M = Harper's Magazine; Harp. W = Harper's Weekly; Int = International; I.S.M = Illustrated Sunday Magazine; L.H.J = Ladies' Home Journal; Lip = Lippincott's Magazine; Lit.R = Little Review; McB = McBride's Magazine; McC = McClure's Magazine; Met = Metropolitan; Mid = Midland; Mir = Reedy's Mirror; Mun = Munsey's Magazine; N.Rep = New Republic; N.S.M = National Sunday Magazine; Outl = Outlook; Pict.R = Pictorial Review; Scr = Scribner's Magazine; S.E.P = Saturday Evening Post; S.S = Smart Set; Smt = Sunset Magazine; W.H.C = Woman's Home Companion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standardized abbreviations when reading or creating index entries to ensure consistency and compactness in the Yearbook's lists.
